_comment: Ask the Bible: questions answered in the Bible's own words. The owner's rule for this box: the framework for interpreting the Bible is the Bible, with no other logic and no scholars' frameworks. So an answer is a `chain` of Scripture and nothing else: 3 to 8 parts, each whole verses (`ref`, at most 3 verses) or `words`, a span of their BSB text copied word for word (at least 3 words). There are no words of ours between the parts, and each part is used only where its own context supports it. `topics` names Nave's Topical Bible subjects (an index only; none of its wording is shown) whose verses form the wider set lit on the map; `only` and `skip` keep or drop labels by prefix, and a top-level label covers its indented lines. `also` lists other ways people ask, for search. `group` is one of the groups in crates/atlas-cli/src/ask.rs. Every part must be tied by the Bible's own data to the question or to another part: it holds the question's words, sits under one of its Nave's subjects, or shares a cross-reference, a quotation (the New Testament quoting the Old, from the BSB's footnotes) or a rarer Hebrew or Greek root with another part. The build checks this and publishes the ties, so the app can show why each verse is there. Links name questions by `id`, so ids never change.
